intent.raw_query: Safari Kenya family of 3, $8000, 10 days, July 2026

experiences.name: Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari
experiences.description: Witness the world-famous Great Migration where millions of wildebeest, zebras, and gazelles cross the Mara River in a dramatic spectacle. Game drives in open 4x4 vehicles offer close encounters with the Big Five including lions, elephants, leopards, buffaloes, and rhinos in their natural habitat.
experiences.location: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County

experiences.name: Amboseli Elephant Watching with Kilimanjaro Backdrop
experiences.description: Observe the largest free-roaming elephant herds in Africa against the stunning backdrop of Mount Kilimanjaro. Amboseli is renowned for its massive tuskers and offers exceptional photography opportunities with swamp ecosystems, diverse birdlife, and Maasai cultural interactions included.

experiences.name: Ol Pejeta Conservancy Rhino Tracking
experiences.description: Track both black and white rhinos on foot or by vehicle at one of Africa's most successful conservation sanctuaries. Home to the last two northern white rhinos on Earth, this experience includes guided bush walks, chimpanzee sanctuary visits, and night game drives revealing nocturnal predators.

experiences.name: Lake Nakuru Flamingo & Bird Safari
experiences.description: Explore the soda lake famous for hosting hundreds of thousands of pink flamingos creating a breathtaking rosy shoreline. The national park also shelters Rothschild giraffes, white rhinos, and over 450 bird species. Scenic viewpoints from the escarpment offer panoramic photography of the entire lake.
experiences.location: Lake Nakuru National Park, Nakuru County

experiences.name: Samburu National Reserve Rare Species Game Drive
experiences.description: Discover the unique Samburu Special Five — Grevy's zebra, reticulated giraffe, Somali ostrich, gerenuk, and Beisa oryx — found nowhere else in Kenya. The Ewaso Ng'iro River running through the reserve attracts dense wildlife concentrations and offers spectacular crocodile and elephant sightings alongside authentic Samburu warrior cultural experiences.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Kenya
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - late night arrival at 22:30. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort and settle in.
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled - in transit.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Nairobi/local airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort, Beachfront Kenya. Complete check-in, freshen up, and get a good night's rest to prepare for the adventure ahead.

meals.breakfast: Meal on flight or skip
meals.lunch: Meal on flight or airport snack
meals.dinner: Light snack from a 24-hour convenience store or hotel welcome snack upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Arrival day only. Pre-arrange airport transfer in advance to save money — shared shuttle services are significantly cheaper than private taxis. Keep some Kenyan Shillings (KES) handy for tips and small expenses. Exchange currency at the airport or use an ATM for better rates.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up and enjoy the beachfront surroundings of the resort. Take a leisurely morning walk along the beach to soak in the warm July weather (25°C). Explore the immediate coastal area, observe local birds and coastal wildlife. Visit a nearby local market to pick up fresh fruit for a budget-friendly breakfast supplement.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to a nearby nature reserve or coastal forest for a self-guided nature walk. Look out for vervet monkeys, colorful birds like sunbirds and kingfishers, and coastal flora. Many smaller reserves along Kenya's coast have low or no entry fees. Alternatively, explore the reef at low tide for marine life spotting.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area. Stroll along the beachfront at sunset — one of Kenya's most spectacular free experiences. Explore local budget eateries (known as 'hotels' locally) near the resort for an authentic Kenyan dinner.

meals.breakfast: Fresh tropical fruit from the local market (mango, pineapple, passion fruit) + chai tea from a roadside vendor — under KES 200
meals.lunch: Local 'mama mboga' food stall — rice, beans, and sukuma wiki (collard greens) for under KES 300
meals.dinner: Local budget restaurant near the beachfront — grilled fish with ugali and kachumbari salad for KES 400-600

day_by_day.notes: July is dry season on the Kenyan coast — excellent weather for outdoor exploration. Wear sunscreen and a hat. Stay hydrated. Avoid exchanging money with street vendors; use official bureaux de change or ATMs.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning birdwatching session along the beach and coastal shrubland near the resort. Kenya's coast is a prime birdwatching destination with species like the Fischer's Turaco, African Fish Eagle, and various waders. Bring binoculars if available. This activity is completely free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby Swahili village or cultural center to learn about coastal Kenyan culture and heritage. Many villages welcome visitors and offer informal tours for a small donation or tip. Explore local craft markets for budget souvenirs — negotiate prices respectfully.
day_by_day.evening: Join a budget group sunset dhow cruise if available locally (traditional wooden sailboat) — typically KES 1,500-2,500 per person for a shared cruise. This is a quintessential coastal Kenya experience. Watch for dolphins that often follow dhows at dusk.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast if included, or local tea house — mandazi (fried dough) and chai for KES 150
meals.lunch: Street food — samosas, bhajias, and fresh coconut water near the village market for under KES 250
meals.dinner: Beachside local eatery — Swahili-style coconut fish curry with rice for KES 500-700

day_by_day.notes: Bargaining is expected at craft markets — start at 50% of the asking price and negotiate respectfully. Carry small denomination notes for street food and tips. The dhow cruise may need to be booked a day in advance through your resort or a local tour operator.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early for a budget day trip to Shimba Hills National Reserve (if staying near the south coast near Diani) or Arabuko-Sokoke Forest Reserve (near Malindi/Watamu area) — one of East Africa's largest coastal forests and a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve. Entry fees are budget-friendly at approximately KES 215 for residents or KES 1,000-1,500 for non-residents. Look for elephants, sable antelopes, and rare birds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the reserve with a self-guided or ranger-led forest walk. Arabuko-Sokoke is home to the endangered Sokoke Scops Owl and Clarke's Weaver. Shimba Hills offers stunning viewpoints and waterfalls. Pack a picnic lunch to save money.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by late afternoon. Rest and freshen up. Explore the evening local food scene — look for nyama choma (roasted meat) joints which are lively, social, and very affordable.

meals.breakfast: Early start — packed mandazi and thermos of tea prepared the night before or from a roadside vendor
meals.lunch: Packed picnic — bread, local cheese, boiled eggs, and fruit purchased from the market the evening before (KES 300-400 total)
meals.dinner: Local nyama choma joint — roasted chicken or goat with kachumbari and ugali for KES 600-900

day_by_day.notes: Book a shared matatu (minibus) or negotiate a shared taxi to the reserve to keep transport costs low. Confirm reserve opening hours and entry fees in advance. Carry insect repellent for the forest. Early morning visits offer the best wildlife sightings.

day_by_day.morning: Take a budget matatu or shared transport to a nearby town for a half-day exploration. Visit the local fresh produce market — a vibrant, colorful experience showcasing local life, tropical fruits, spices, and crafts. This is a fantastic free cultural immersion activity.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local conservation project or community wildlife sanctuary. Many coastal Kenya communities run small but impactful conservation programs with very affordable entry. Learn about sea turtle conservation, marine life protection, or local elephant corridors. Some programs allow volunteer participation for a few hours.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area. Enjoy a free beach sunset walk. Try a local 'kibanda' (small roadside eatery) for dinner — these are the most authentic and budget-friendly dining options in Kenya.

meals.breakfast: Local tea house near the market — fried eggs, bread, and chai for KES 200-300
meals.lunch: Market food stalls — pilau rice (spiced rice) with beef for KES 250-350
meals.dinner: Kibanda dinner — beans stew, rice, and vegetable curry for KES 200-350

day_by_day.notes: Matatus are the most affordable public transport in Kenya — agree on the fare before boarding. Keep your belongings secure in busy market areas. Community conservation projects appreciate small donations and purchases of locally made crafts.

day_by_day.morning: Full day safari preparation and early departure for a budget safari experience. Head to Tsavo East or Tsavo West National Park — two of Kenya's largest and most accessible national parks, offering excellent wildlife viewing at relatively lower costs than Masai Mara. Arrange a budget group safari through a local operator (shared game drives significantly reduce costs). Look for elephants, lions, leopards, buffalos, and giraffes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Afternoon game drive continuing through the park. Tsavo is famous for its large red-dust elephants and the Lugard Falls on the Galana River in Tsavo East. Keep cameras ready — afternoon light is ideal for wildlife photography. Enjoy a packed lunch at a designated picnic site inside the park.
day_by_day.evening: Return from the park by late afternoon/early evening. Rest at the resort. Share safari stories and photos over a relaxed dinner.

meals.breakfast: Very early breakfast — resort or packed bread with peanut butter and bananas for energy
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at park picnic site — sandwiches, fruit, and juice (prepared the evening before)
meals.dinner: Resort dinner or local restaurant — treat yourself slightly after a big safari day — grilled tilapia with chips for KES 700-900

day_by_day.notes: Book the safari group tour 2-3 days in advance through your resort or a reputable local budget operator. Tsavo park fees are approximately USD 52 per person per day for non-residents (2027 estimated). Sharing a safari vehicle with 5-6 people dramatically reduces per-person costs. Wear neutral-colored clothing (khaki, olive, brown) for game drives.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning after the safari day. Enjoy a slow morning at the beachfront resort. Take a morning swim in the Indian Ocean — warm, calm July waters are perfect. Explore tide pools along the beach for starfish, sea urchins, and small fish.
day_by_day.afternoon: Snorkeling excursion at a nearby coral reef — Kenya's coast has spectacular coral gardens teeming with tropical fish. Rent basic snorkel gear locally (KES 500-800) or join a budget group snorkeling trip. Marine National Parks like Watamu or Malindi Marine Reserve offer incredible underwater wildlife experiences.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset beach bonfire if permitted at the resort area, or join locals for an evening of music and socializing. Look for free or low-cost live taarab or benga music performances at local venues.

meals.breakfast: Relaxed resort breakfast or fresh fruit smoothie from a beachside vendor — KES 300-400
meals.lunch: Beach shack seafood — grilled calamari or prawns with chips for KES 500-700
meals.dinner: Local restaurant — Swahili biryani (fragrant spiced rice with meat) for KES 500-650

day_by_day.notes: Always snorkel with a buddy and be aware of currents. The marine park entry fee is separate from snorkel gear rental. Avoid touching or standing on coral reefs — they are fragile and protected ecosystems. July's calm Indian Ocean conditions make this an ideal snorkeling day.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning nature walk or cycling tour through coastal hinterland villages and farmland. Many local guides offer budget walking tours for KES 500-1,000 per person. Observe rural Kenyan life, local farming practices, and spot wildlife such as monitor lizards, mongoose, and colorful butterflies.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local eco-lodge or conservation education center for a guided talk on Kenyan wildlife and conservation efforts. Many such centers are free or charge a small donation. Spend the later afternoon relaxing at the beach or resort pool.
day_by_day.evening: Cooking class with a local family or community group — learn to make Swahili coastal dishes like pilau, biryani, or coconut bean soup. These experiences are often very affordable (KES 1,000-2,000) and include dinner. A wonderful cultural immersion activity.

meals.breakfast: Roadside vendor — chapati with egg and tea for KES 150-200
meals.lunch: Village home-cooked meal if offered during the walking tour, or packed lunch from the market
meals.dinner: Cooking class dinner — eat what you cook! Included in the class cost

day_by_day.notes: Ask your resort reception to recommend trusted local guides for the walking/cycling tour. Cooking classes can be arranged through community tourism groups or your resort. This is one of the most memorable and budget-friendly cultural experiences available.

day_by_day.morning: Final full day — make the most of it with an early morning kayaking session along the coastline. Budget kayak rentals are available at most Kenyan beach resorts for KES 500-800 per hour. Paddle along mangrove channels if available — mangroves are incredible ecosystems home to crabs, mudskippers, herons, and kingfishers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local wildlife orphanage or rescue center if one is nearby. These centers rehabilitate injured or orphaned wildlife including bushbabies, monkeys, and birds of prey. Entry fees are typically very affordable and directly support conservation. Spend the remaining afternoon doing last-minute souvenir shopping at the local market.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at the best local budget restaurant you've discovered during the trip. Celebrate the incredible 10-day Kenya adventure. Watch the final Indian Ocean sunset from the beach.

meals.breakfast: Special farewell breakfast — treat yourself to a slightly bigger meal at a local café — full Kenyan breakfast with eggs, sausage, bread, and chai for KES 400-500
meals.lunch: Light lunch — fresh coconut and tropical fruit platter from the beach market for KES 200-300
meals.dinner: Best local restaurant of the trip — full Swahili seafood feast: grilled lobster or crab if budget allows (KES 1,000-1,500) or stick to grilled fish for KES 600-800

day_by_day.notes: Pack souvenirs carefully — wooden carvings, Maasai beadwork, and Kikoi fabric are popular and lightweight options. Declare any wildlife products (shells, corals) at customs — many are restricted. Confirm departure logistics for the following day.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Kenya. Wake up for one last sunrise beach walk — a peaceful and free farewell to the Kenyan coast. Pack and prepare for checkout. Double-check all belongings and travel documents.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Depending on departure flight time, use remaining hours for a final stroll through the local area, any last souvenir purchases, or simply relaxing at a beachside café with a fresh juice. Arrange shared shuttle or matatu to the airport well in advance.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Kenya with incredible memories of safari adventures, coastal wildlife, warm Swahili hospitality, and spectacular Indian Ocean sunsets. Safe travels!

meals.breakfast: Final Kenyan breakfast — mandazi, chai, and fresh mango at a local tea house for KES 200
meals.lunch: Airport or town café — light meal before departure for KES 400-600
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at the airport at least 3 hours before international departure. Keep KES 1,000-2,000 in cash for airport tips, last-minute snacks, and unforeseen expenses. Most Kenyan airports have currency exchange counters to convert remaining Shillings back. Take only memories and leave only footprints — Kenya's wildlife and ecosystems depend on responsible tourism.

trip_options.title: Classic Kenya Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Clear immigration, collect luggage, and meet your pre-arranged transfer driver. Transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort (approximately 1–2 hours depending on traffic). Check in, freshen up, and settle into your beachfront accommodation.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — in-flight or airport meal
meals.lunch: Not applicable — in-flight or airport meal
meals.dinner: Light late-night snack or welcome drink at the resort's 24-hour lounge upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange airport pickup with the resort in advance. Keep essentials in your carry-on for a smooth late-night check-in. Exchange some currency to Kenyan Shillings (KES) at the airport forex bureau. Get a good night's rest — your adventure begins tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely resort breakfast. Spend the morning exploring the Aegean Bliss Resort grounds and beachfront. Take a relaxing walk along the Kenyan coastline, acclimate to the warm 25°C weather, and orient yourself with the local surroundings. Visit the resort's information desk to confirm upcoming safari bookings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a guided cultural walk to a nearby local village or market to experience Kenyan coastal culture and Swahili heritage. Browse handcrafted souvenirs, fresh tropical fruits, and local spices. This gentle half-day introduction eases you into the trip without overexertion after your late arrival.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a sundowner on the beachfront terrace watching the Indian Ocean sunset. Attend the resort's optional cultural evening featuring traditional Kenyan music and dance performance.

meals.breakfast: Full buffet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort restaurant — enjoy fresh tropical fruits, eggs, and Kenyan chai tea
meals.lunch: Casual beachside lunch at the resort's beach bar — try grilled tilapia or pilau rice (mid-range, ~KES 800–1,200)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a well-regarded local coastal restaurant near the resort — try Swahili-style coconut fish curry and ugali (~KES 1,500–2,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Stay hydrated in the warm summer heat. Apply sunscreen generously. Confirm your Day 3 transfer to Maasai Mara with the resort concierge. Tip: The warm July weather is perfect for early morning and late afternoon outdoor activities.

day_by_day.morning: Early departure by road or chartered light aircraft transfer to Maasai Mara National Reserve (flight ~45 min, road ~5–6 hours). Check in to your mid-range tented camp inside or bordering the Mara ecosystem. After settling in, enjoy an orientation briefing from your safari guide about the Great Migration and reserve rules.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin your first Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari game drive. Witness millions of wildebeest, zebras, and Thomson's gazelles moving across the golden savannah. Look out for predators — lions, cheetahs, and leopards — that follow the migration herds. Cross into the Mara Triangle area for prime wildlife viewing.
day_by_day.evening: Return to camp as the sun sets over the Mara plains. Enjoy a campfire bush dinner under the stars with fellow travelers and your guide sharing stories of the day's sightings.

meals.breakfast: Early packed breakfast or quick continental breakfast at the resort before departure
meals.lunch: Bush picnic lunch prepared by your safari camp served in the field during the game drive — sandwiches, fruit, and juice
meals.dinner: Three-course dinner at the tented camp dining area — expect Kenyan stew, roasted vegetables, and fresh bread (~included in most mid-range camp packages)

day_by_day.notes: Pack warm layers — early morning game drives can be cool at 15–18°C on the Mara. Bring binoculars, a camera with zoom lens, and insect repellent. July is peak Great Migration season — river crossings at the Mara River are a highlight. Book a specific river crossing game drive with your guide.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn wake-up for a sunrise game drive in the Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari. The golden morning light offers spectacular photography opportunities. Focus on the Mara River crossing points where wildebeest brave crocodile-filled waters in dramatic fashion — one of nature's greatest spectacles.
day_by_day.afternoon: Optional hot air balloon safari over the Mara ecosystem (premium add-on, ~USD 450–500 per person) for a bird's-eye view of the migration herds stretching to the horizon. Alternatively, enjoy a guided nature walk on the Mara conservancy with a Maasai warrior guide to learn about local flora, tracking skills, and Maasai culture.
day_by_day.evening: Visit a traditional Maasai village (manyatta) for a cultural immersion experience. Participate in traditional dances, learn about Maasai customs, and purchase authentic beaded jewelry directly from artisans. Return to camp for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early hot thermos of tea/coffee and light snacks before the sunrise drive; full cooked breakfast served at camp upon return
meals.lunch: Lunch at the camp — fresh salads, grilled meats, and seasonal vegetables
meals.dinner: Barbecue bush dinner at camp with nyama choma (roasted meat) and traditional Kenyan sides

day_by_day.notes: The Mara River crossings are unpredictable — patience is key. Ask your guide for the best crossing points based on herd movements that day. The Maasai village visit typically costs ~KES 2,000–3,000 per person and goes directly to the community.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning game drive in Maasai Mara focusing on big cat sightings — lions with cubs, leopards in acacia trees, and cheetahs on termite mounds. The Mara is home to one of Africa's highest densities of big cats, making every drive rewarding.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out from the Mara tented camp and transfer by chartered light aircraft or road to Ol Pejeta Conservancy in the Laikipia Plateau. Check in to your mid-range lodge inside or near the conservancy. Rest and freshen up after travel.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a sunset game drive around Ol Pejeta Conservancy's perimeter to spot resident wildlife including elephants, buffalos, and the famous resident chimpanzee sanctuary. Brief evening introduction from the conservancy ranger about the rhino tracking program.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the Mara camp before checkout
meals.lunch: Packed lunch during transfer or light meal at a roadside stop en route to Ol Pejeta (~KES 600–900)
meals.dinner: Dinner at the Ol Pejeta lodge restaurant — try Kenyan-style beef stew with chapati and fresh vegetable sides (~KES 1,800–2,500)

day_by_day.notes: Ol Pejeta is home to the world's last two northern white rhinos (Najin and Fatu) — a deeply moving conservation experience. Transfers between parks are best done by light aircraft to save time. Confirm your rhino tracking booking upon arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning Ol Pejeta Conservancy Rhino Tracking experience. Track both black and white rhinos on foot or by vehicle with an expert ranger and anti-poaching team. Learn about the intensive conservation efforts protecting these critically endangered animals. Visit the enclosure of Najin and Fatu, the last northern white rhinos on Earth.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Ol Pejeta Chimpanzee Sanctuary — the only place in Kenya where you can see chimpanzees rescued from across Africa. Afterward, enjoy a self-guided or guided game drive to spot lions, leopards, zebras, and large elephant herds that roam freely across the conservancy's 90,000 acres.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner drinks on the conservancy plains with panoramic views of Mount Kenya's snow-capped peaks glowing in the evening light. Return to the lodge for a relaxed dinner and conservation talk by a resident ranger.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the lodge before rhino tracking
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch in the conservancy or at the lodge veranda — sandwiches, fresh juice, and local fruits
meals.dinner: Dinner at the lodge — enjoy a three-course meal with Kenyan-inspired dishes and a glass of local Leleshwa wine (~KES 2,000–3,000)

day_by_day.notes: Rhino tracking on foot requires a moderate level of fitness and closed-toe shoes. Follow all ranger instructions carefully for safety. Photography guidelines apply near the northern white rhinos — respect their space. Ol Pejeta's conservation fee (~USD 90/day) is included in most mid-range packages.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Ol Pejeta and transfer to Lake Nakuru National Park (approximately 2–3 hours by road through the scenic Rift Valley escarpment). Arrive and check in to a mid-range lodge near the lake. Begin the Lake Nakuru Flamingo & Bird Safari immediately after lunch briefing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Embark on a full Lake Nakuru game drive. The alkaline soda lake hosts hundreds of thousands of lesser and greater flamingos creating a breathtaking pink shoreline. Also spot white and black rhinos (Lake Nakuru is a rhino sanctuary), Rothschild's giraffes, buffalos, and an extraordinary diversity of 450+ bird species.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a sundowner at a scenic viewpoint overlooking Lake Nakuru with the flamingo-pink lake shimmering below. Return to the lodge for dinner. Spend the evening reviewing wildlife photographs and journaling the day's extraordinary sightings.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Ol Pejeta lodge before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at a roadside restaurant en route to Lake Nakuru — try githeri (maize and beans) or a local Kenyan buffet (~KES 700–1,000)
meals.dinner: Dinner at the Lake Nakuru lodge — fresh lake tilapia, ugali, and sukuma wiki (collard greens) (~KES 1,500–2,200)

day_by_day.notes: Lake Nakuru's flamingo numbers fluctuate with water levels — July typically offers excellent viewing. Bring a telephoto lens for bird photography. The park also offers excellent leopard sightings in the fever tree forests. Keep vehicle windows partially closed near baboon areas.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning game drive in Lake Nakuru National Park focusing on the lion pride and leopard population in the forested areas. The cool morning air makes predators especially active. Visit the waterfall and viewpoints for panoramic Rift Valley photography.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer from Lake Nakuru to Amboseli National Park (approximately 4–5 hours by road or 1 hour by light aircraft). Arrive and check in to your mid-range Amboseli lodge or tented camp. Freshen up and enjoy a late afternoon game drive to catch the legendary Kilimanjaro sunset.
day_by_day.evening: Witness the iconic Amboseli scene — massive elephant bulls silhouetted against Mount Kilimanjaro as the sky turns orange and pink at dusk. This is one of Africa's most photographed wildlife moments. Enjoy a relaxed lodge dinner recounting the day's journey.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at Lake Nakuru lodge before checkout
meals.lunch: Packed lunch during road transfer or quick stop at a local eatery in Naivasha (~KES 800–1,200)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Amboseli lodge — Kenyan cuisine with a view of the Kilimanjaro silhouette from the dining terrace (~KES 2,000–2,800)

day_by_day.notes: Amboseli is best accessed via light aircraft from Nakuru or Nairobi Wilson Airport to save significant travel time. If driving, the C103 road through Namanga is scenic but long. Kilimanjaro is most visible in the early morning before clouds form — set your alarm early for Day 9.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn wake-up for the Amboseli Elephant Watching with Kilimanjaro Backdrop experience at sunrise. The crystal-clear July air and warm summer weather offer the best Kilimanjaro visibility of the year. Observe the largest free-roaming elephant herds in Africa — families of 50+ elephants crossing the swamps with Africa's highest peak as a dramatic backdrop. Your guide will introduce you to individually identified elephant families studied by the Amboseli Elephant Research Project.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the elephant-focused game drive through Amboseli's diverse ecosystems — open plains, acacia woodlands, and papyrus swamps. Spot lions, cheetahs, hyenas, zebras, wildebeest, and over 400 bird species. Visit the Observation Hill for a panoramic 360-degree view of the entire Amboseli basin.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a special sundowner bush dinner set up in the open plains by your lodge team — tables, candles, and lanterns under the vast African sky with Kilimanjaro glowing in the last light. This is a quintessential mid-range safari splurge worth every shilling.

meals.breakfast: Thermos coffee and light snacks before sunrise drive; full hot breakfast served at camp upon return
meals.lunch: Lunch at the lodge — fresh salads, grilled chicken, and tropical fruit (~included in lodge package)
meals.dinner: Special bush dinner in the Amboseli plains — three-course meal with wine under the stars (~KES 3,500–5,000 per person as an add-on)

day_by_day.notes: Amboseli's elephant population is habituated to vehicles — you can get remarkably close for photography. Respect the 20-meter minimum distance rule. The Amboseli Elephant Research Project has tracked these herds since 1972 — ask your guide about specific family groups. Dust can be significant — bring a buff or scarf.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise game drive in Amboseli for last elephant and Kilimanjaro sightings. Pack up and check out of the lodge. Transfer back to Nairobi (approximately 4 hours by road or 45-minute flight). If time allows, stop at the Karen Blixen Museum or Giraffe Centre in Nairobi's Karen suburb for a memorable urban wildlife encounter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive back in Nairobi. Visit the Nairobi Giraffe Centre to hand-feed endangered Rothschild's giraffes — a wonderful final wildlife experience. Explore the nearby Kazuri Beads factory for fair-trade souvenirs handmade by local women artisans. Head to the city center or Westlands for last-minute shopping at Maasai Market.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at one of Nairobi's celebrated mid-range restaurants. Carnivore Restaurant is a Nairobi institution offering an all-you-can-eat nyama choma experience with exotic meats and traditional sides — perfect for a celebratory last night. Transfer to Jomo Kenyatta International Airport for your departure flight.

meals.breakfast: Final lodge breakfast at Amboseli before checkout
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a Nairobi café in Karen or Westlands — try Java House Kenya for a reliable mid-range meal (~KES 1,000–1,500)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Carnivore Restaurant, Nairobi — iconic Kenyan dining experience (~KES 3,500–5,000 per person including drinks)

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your departure flight time and allow at least 3 hours for international check-in at JKIA. Keep USD or KES for airport taxes and last-minute purchases. Declare any wildlife products (leather, feathers) at customs — purchase only certified legal souvenirs. Asante sana (thank you very much) — Kenya will stay with you forever!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Kenya Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari
experiences.description: Witness the world-famous Great Migration where millions of wildebeest, zebras, and gazelles cross the Mara River in a dramatic spectacle. Game drives in open 4x4 vehicles offer close encounters with the Big Five including lions, elephants, leopards, buffaloes, and rhinos in their natural habitat.
experiences.location: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County

experiences.name: Amboseli Elephant Watching with Kilimanjaro Backdrop
experiences.description: Observe the largest free-roaming elephant herds in Africa against the stunning backdrop of Mount Kilimanjaro. Amboseli is renowned for its massive tuskers and offers exceptional photography opportunities with swamp ecosystems, diverse birdlife, and Maasai cultural interactions included.

experiences.name: Ol Pejeta Conservancy Rhino Tracking
experiences.description: Track both black and white rhinos on foot or by vehicle at one of Africa's most successful conservation sanctuaries. Home to the last two northern white rhinos on Earth, this experience includes guided bush walks, chimpanzee sanctuary visits, and night game drives revealing nocturnal predators.

experiences.name: Lake Nakuru Flamingo & Bird Safari
experiences.description: Explore the soda lake famous for hosting hundreds of thousands of pink flamingos creating a breathtaking rosy shoreline. The national park also shelters Rothschild giraffes, white rhinos, and over 450 bird species. Scenic viewpoints from the escarpment offer panoramic photography of the entire lake.
experiences.location: Lake Nakuru National Park, Nakuru County

experiences.name: Samburu National Reserve Rare Species Game Drive
experiences.description: Discover the unique Samburu Special Five — Grevy's zebra, reticulated giraffe, Somali ostrich, gerenuk, and Beisa oryx — found nowhere else in Kenya. The Ewaso Ng'iro River running through the reserve attracts dense wildlife concentrations and offers spectacular crocodile and elephant sightings alongside authentic Samburu warrior cultural experiences.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late night arrival at 22:30 on Flight UA. Private luxury transfer from Nairobi Jomo Kenyatta International Airport to Aegean Bliss Resort with a dedicated meet-and-greet concierge service.
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — travel day.
day_by_day.evening: Late-night welcome at Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy a complimentary arrival cocktail and light gourmet snack prepared by the resort's private chef. Check-in to your beachfront suite and unwind with a brief orientation from your personal butler.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — arrival after 22:30
meals.lunch: Not applicable — in-flight or airport dining
meals.dinner: Late-night welcome platter at Aegean Bliss Resort: artisan charcuterie, fresh tropical fruits, and Kenyan craft beer or premium wine selection served in-suite

day_by_day.notes: Arrival is at 22:30 — no daytime activities planned. Ensure all safari gear and luggage is organized tonight for an early start tomorrow. Confirm private driver and bush-plane bookings with the concierge upon check-in.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely late breakfast at the resort to recover from travel. Enjoy a guided beachfront nature walk along the Kenyan coast with a resident naturalist, spotting coastal bird species, mangroves, and marine life in tidal pools. Light stretching and yoga session on the private beach deck optional.
day_by_day.afternoon: Resort orientation and leisure time. Explore the resort's private grounds, take a dip in the infinity pool overlooking the Indian Ocean, and meet with your personal safari concierge to confirm the full 10-day itinerary, logistics, and packing essentials for upcoming bush adventures.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset sundowner cocktails on the beachfront terrace. Enjoy a formal welcome dinner at the resort's signature restaurant featuring a curated Kenyan coastal tasting menu with fresh seafood and locally sourced ingredients.

meals.breakfast: Lavish buffet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — fresh tropical fruits, Kenyan chai, eggs made to order, smoked fish, and freshly baked pastries
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch — grilled prawns, avocado salad, and fresh coconut water served at the resort's beach cabana
meals.dinner: Signature tasting menu at the resort's fine dining restaurant — Swahili-spiced lobster bisque, grilled barracuda with coconut pilau, and passion fruit panna cotta paired with South African Chenin Blanc

day_by_day.notes: Use this day as a gentle recovery day after the late arrival. Confirm all upcoming internal flight and safari camp transfers with the concierge. Pack a dedicated safari bag for bush camps — light, neutral-colored clothing recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Early private charter flight from the coast to Amboseli National Park (approximately 1.5-hour scenic flight). Upon landing, transfer to your luxury tented camp. Begin the Amboseli Elephant Watching with Kilimanjaro Backdrop experience — a guided morning game drive to observe the largest free-roaming elephant herds in Africa with the iconic snow-capped Mount Kilimanjaro as a dramatic backdrop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Extended afternoon game drive through Amboseli's open savannah plains. Spot large elephant matriarchal herds, Cape buffalo, lions, cheetahs, and hundreds of bird species including crowned cranes and saddle-billed storks. Visit a Maasai cultural boma for an exclusive private interaction and traditional dance performance.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the luxury tented camp for bush sundowners around a fire pit under the African sky. Enjoy a private bush dinner under the stars with lantern lighting and Maasai warrior storytelling.

meals.breakfast: Early pre-flight breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — energy-packed continental spread with Kenyan coffee and fresh juice
meals.lunch: Gourmet bush picnic lunch in the field — smoked chicken wraps, quinoa salad, fresh fruit, and chilled sparkling water served from a luxury hamper
meals.dinner: Private candlelit bush dinner at camp — slow-braised Kenyan lamb shank, roasted root vegetables, and malva pudding with Amarula cream, paired with Kenyan Pinot Noir

day_by_day.notes: Amboseli is best visited early morning and late afternoon for optimal Kilimanjaro visibility before clouds build. Bring a high-quality camera with a telephoto lens. July is dry season — dust can be significant, bring a buff or light scarf.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise hot air balloon flight over Amboseli's plains — a breathtaking panoramic view of elephant herds, Kilimanjaro, and the vast savannah at dawn. Champagne breakfast served in the bush upon landing, a classic African luxury experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Guided walking safari with an expert Maasai tracker — explore the ecosystem on foot, tracking wildlife signs, learning about medicinal plants, and observing smaller fauna often missed on vehicle drives. Visit the Observation Hill for sweeping 360-degree views of the park.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell sundowners at the camp's elevated viewing deck. Relax with a signature spa treatment at the camp — traditional Kenyan massage using local oils and herbs. Prepare for tomorrow's transfer to the Maasai Mara.

meals.breakfast: Champagne bush breakfast in the field following the balloon flight — smoked salmon, scrambled eggs, fresh pastries, tropical fruit platters, and Moët & Chandon
meals.lunch: Leisurely lunch at camp — grilled tilapia with mango salsa, roasted sweet potato, and a refreshing hibiscus iced tea
meals.dinner: Communal camp dinner with fellow guests — three-course menu featuring Kenyan beef tenderloin, sautéed greens, and a decadent chocolate tart with local honey drizzle

day_by_day.notes: Hot air balloon must be pre-booked and is weather dependent. Wear warm layers for the early morning balloon flight as temperatures at altitude can be cool. Confirm Maasai Mara charter flight for the following morning with camp management.

day_by_day.morning: Private charter flight from Amboseli to Maasai Mara National Reserve (approximately 1-hour flight). Check in to your ultra-luxury tented camp on the Mara. Begin the Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari — an exhilarating morning game drive to witness millions of wildebeest, zebras, and gazelles in their annual migration across the Mara River ecosystem.
day_by_day.afternoon: Position at the Mara River crossing points with your expert guide for the spectacular and dramatic wildebeest river crossings — one of nature's greatest wildlife spectacles. Observe massive crocodiles, hippos, and predators including lions and leopards hunting along the riverbanks.
day_by_day.evening: Return to camp for a bush sundowner cocktail experience at a private scenic viewpoint. Enjoy a lavish dinner at the camp's main lodge with live traditional Maasai music performance.

meals.breakfast: Pre-flight breakfast at Amboseli camp — full English bush breakfast with Kenyan sausages, eggs, grilled tomatoes, and strong Kenyan AA coffee
meals.lunch: Bush picnic lunch at the Mara River — gourmet sandwiches, cold cuts, artisan cheeses, and fresh-squeezed juices served riverside
meals.dinner: Gala camp dinner — flame-grilled Mara game meat platter (optional), roasted vegetable tower, and a decadent Kenyan coffee crème brûlée paired with a premium Cabernet Sauvignon

day_by_day.notes: July is peak Great Migration season — river crossings are highly likely but not guaranteed as they depend on wildebeest movement. Patience at the river is key. Bring binoculars, sunscreen, and a hat. The Mara can be dusty — a camera lens cloth is essential.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day exclusive private game drive in the Maasai Mara with a dedicated expert guide and luxury Land Cruiser. Morning focus on the Big Five — lion prides, leopards in acacia trees, elephants, Cape buffalo, and black rhinos. Visit the Mara Triangle for less-crowded wildlife viewing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Afternoon continuation of the private game drive. Seek out cheetah hunts on the open plains — July offers exceptional cheetah sightings. Stop at a scenic kopje for an afternoon tea break with panoramic savannah views.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive private bush dinner set up in the open Mara plains under a canopy of stars — white linen, silver cutlery, and a personal chef. A truly once-in-a-lifetime dining experience surrounded by the sounds of the African bush.

meals.breakfast: Full camp breakfast — fresh fruit, granola with Kenyan honey, eggs Benedict with smoked salmon, and freshly brewed Kenyan coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet field lunch served from the vehicle — artisan baguettes, cold poached chicken, caprese salad, and chilled sparkling water
meals.dinner: Private open-air bush dinner on the Mara plains — five-course menu featuring Kenyan-spiced rack of lamb, truffle risotto, and a dark chocolate fondant with vanilla bean ice cream, paired with a premium South African red blend

day_by_day.notes: A full private game drive day maximizes wildlife sightings and flexibility. Request your guide to focus on predator activity reports from the morning ranger briefing. Dress in layers — mornings can be cool at 15°C before warming to 25°C by midday.

day_by_day.morning: Private charter flight from Maasai Mara to Ol Pejeta Conservancy (approximately 1.5-hour flight). Check in to your luxury lodge. Begin the Ol Pejeta Conservancy Rhino Tracking experience — a guided foot safari with armed rangers to track both endangered black and white rhinos, including a visit to see the last northern white rhinos on the planet.
day_by_day.afternoon: Afternoon game drive through Ol Pejeta's diverse ecosystem — spot lions, leopards, cheetahs, and the Sweetwaters Chimpanzee Sanctuary, the only place in Kenya to see rescued chimpanzees. Enjoy an exclusive guided conservation talk with a resident wildlife researcher.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner drinks at the conservancy's scenic viewpoint overlooking Mount Kenya. Dinner at the lodge's fine dining restaurant with a focus on conservation-to-table cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Light pre-flight breakfast at the Mara camp — fresh fruit, yogurt, and Kenyan tea
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Ol Pejeta lodge upon arrival — grilled chicken with roasted vegetables, garden salad, and freshly squeezed passion fruit juice
meals.dinner: Fine dining at the lodge — pan-seared duck breast with a Kenyan berry reduction, wild mushroom risotto, and a lemon tart with Chantilly cream, paired with a premium Burgundy

day_by_day.notes: The northern white rhino experience at Ol Pejeta is profoundly moving — only two remain on Earth (both female). This is a critical conservation site. Photography is encouraged to raise awareness. Wear sturdy walking boots for the rhino tracking foot safari.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning game drive at Ol Pejeta with a focus on lion and leopard activity. The conservancy is renowned for its high predator density. Visit the black rhino enclosure for a close-up educational session with the head rhino keeper — an exclusive behind-the-scenes conservation experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private charter flight from Ol Pejeta to Lake Nakuru National Park (approximately 45-minute flight). Check in to your luxury lodge overlooking the lake. Begin the Lake Nakuru Flamingo and Bird Safari — witness hundreds of thousands of pink flamingos creating a breathtaking pink carpet across the soda lake shoreline.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset game drive around Lake Nakuru — spot white rhinos, Rothschild giraffes, lions, and a rich diversity of over 400 bird species. Return to the lodge for a lakeside dinner.

meals.breakfast: Full lodge breakfast at Ol Pejeta — eggs your way, Kenyan sausages, fresh tropical fruit, and strong Kenyan AA coffee
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch at Lake Nakuru upon arrival — smoked trout, artisan crackers, fresh salads, and chilled white wine
meals.dinner: Lakeside dinner at the Nakuru lodge — Kenyan-style tilapia in coconut sauce, steamed jasmine rice, and a decadent mango cheesecake, paired with a crisp Sauvignon Blanc

day_by_day.notes: Lake Nakuru flamingo numbers fluctuate with water levels — July typically offers spectacular sightings. The lake is also a sanctuary for both black and white rhinos. Bring a wide-angle lens for flamingo panoramas and a telephoto for bird close-ups.

day_by_day.morning: Private charter flight from Lake Nakuru to Samburu National Reserve (approximately 1-hour flight). Check in to your luxury tented camp on the banks of the Ewaso Ng'iro River. Begin the Samburu National Reserve Rare Species Game Drive — discover the unique Samburu Special Five: Grevy's zebra, reticulated giraffe, Somali ostrich, gerenuk, and Beisa oryx, found nowhere else in Kenya.
day_by_day.afternoon: Afternoon game drive along the riverbanks — spot large crocodiles, elephants crossing the river, and leopards resting in doum palms. Engage in an exclusive cultural experience with local Samburu warriors — learn about their traditions, beadwork, and semi-nomadic lifestyle.
day_by_day.evening: Riverside sundowner cocktails with the sounds of the African bush. Private dinner at the camp with a Samburu cultural storytelling performance around a traditional fire.

meals.breakfast: Pre-flight breakfast at Nakuru lodge — continental spread with fresh fruits, yogurt, and Kenyan chai
meals.lunch: Welcome lunch at Samburu camp — grilled chicken skewers, roasted corn, fresh tomato salad, and homemade lemonade
meals.dinner: Private camp dinner — slow-cooked Samburu-style goat stew with ugali, sautéed sukuma wiki, and a coconut milk rice pudding with cardamom, paired with a premium Kenyan craft gin cocktail

day_by_day.notes: Samburu is a remote and wild reserve — one of Kenya's most authentic safari destinations. The Samburu Special Five are genuinely unique to this ecosystem. The Ewaso Ng'iro River is a magnet for wildlife, especially in the dry season. Evening game drives offer excellent leopard sightings.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise game drive in Samburu — a last opportunity to photograph the rare Samburu Special Five and observe elephant herds crossing the river at dawn. Return to camp for a celebratory farewell breakfast with the camp team.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private charter flight back to the coast (approximately 2-hour flight) returning to Aegean Bliss Resort. Afternoon of pure luxury — rejuvenating spa treatment featuring a full-body Kenyan coffee scrub and deep tissue massage, followed by a leisurely swim in the infinity pool overlooking the Indian Ocean.
day_by_day.evening: Grand farewell gala dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort's premium beachfront restaurant — a curated celebration of Kenyan cuisine and culture. Reflect on an extraordinary 10-day journey over a spectacular multi-course dinner with fine wine, live Swahili coastal music, and a personalized memory book prepared by the resort team.

meals.breakfast: Farewell bush breakfast at Samburu camp — full spread with fresh fruits, eggs, Kenyan sausages, honey, and camp-brewed coffee
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch at Aegean Bliss Resort upon return — grilled lobster tail, avocado and mango salad, and a chilled glass of Rosé
meals.dinner: Grand farewell tasting menu at Aegean Bliss Resort — Kenyan coastal crab cakes, Swahili-spiced beef tenderloin, truffle-infused ugali, and a decadent chocolate and Kenyan coffee fondant, paired with a curated wine flight featuring South African and French selections

day_by_day.notes: Arrange departure transfers and any additional luggage storage with the resort concierge. Request a personalized highlight photo book or USB from the camp photographers as a keepsake. Confirm onward departure flights and ensure all safari souvenirs comply with customs regulations — no wildlife products permitted.
